title.narrative: Greater Mekong Subregion Tourism Infrastructure for Inclusive Growth Project

description.narrative: The project will remove physical and capacity constraints impeding tourism development in Champassak, Khammouane, Luangprabang, and Oudomxay - four provinces situated astride the GMS Central Corridor. It will contribute to the creation of 27,000 tourism-related jobs in the Lao PDR by: (i) paving 70 kilometers (km) of rural roads to open new areas for private tourism investment and improve access to markets and social services for 15,000 people; (ii) improving environmental services in areas important for cross-border tourism to reduce public health hazards for 35,000 residents and 2.4 million annual visitors, beginning in 2019; and (iii) facilitating business support services for at least 500 small and medium-sized enterprises.3 The project will strengthen regional cooperation and integration by implementing regional tourism standards, promoting multicountry tour circuits, and supporting structured policy dialogue to reduce nonphysical barriers to travel. The project investment plan is in line with the GMS Tourism Sector Strategy,4 and the government's National Tourism Strategy, 2012-2020.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Increased tourism receipts in Champassak, Khammouane, Luangprabang, and Oudomxay

Aggregate annual tourism receipts in the 4 project provinces equals $330 million. (2012 baseline: $160 million) Achievement: not available Progress/Status: - The aggregated annual tourism receipts in the target provinces increased from $160 million in 2012 to $464 million in 2019 (target: $330 million). However, the tourism sector has been greatly affected by the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic in 2020 and 2021 and the revenue dropped below the target in 2020 and 2021. Data Source: - MICT Tourism Statistics Report - Completion report. Actual value: not available
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Effective project implementation and knowledge management. Indicator: 12 new knowledge products published to Lao PDR's web-based tourism knowledge center. Achievement: 36 Progress/Status: Achieved. 32 knowledge products uploaded to date. http://www.tiigp-laos.org/other.html. Data Source: Project progress reports. End of project impact evaluation.

Output: Effective project implementation and knowledge management. Indicator: 20% of tourism enterprises in the 4 project provinces meet ASEAN tourism standards. Achievement: 28 Progress/Status: Achieved. The project's focus for ASEAN Tourism Standards implementation was on ASEAN Community Based Tourism Standard, ASEAN Homestay Standard and ASEAN Green Hotel Standards.
Overall, 42 (20.7%) of 203 enterprises have been certified.
The breakdown by standard for certification in the four target provinces is as follows:
- 2 (18%) out of a total of 11 homestay villages in the target provinces received ASEAN Homestay Standard certificate. - 3 (25%) out of a total of 12 CBT operations in the target provinces received ASEAN Community-based Tourism Standard certificate. - 37 (21%) out of a total of 180 hotels in the target provinces certified under the ASEAN Green Hotel Standard.
In addition to the above-listed enterprises, the project has also supported 3 public toilets to meet criteria for the ASEAN Public Toilet Standard certification (2 in Champasak province and 1 in Luang Prabang province). Data Source: Project progress reports. GMS TWG Summary of Proceedings

Output: Effective project implementation and knowledge management. Indicator: At least 30% of PCU and PIU staff are women Achievement: 33 Progress/Status: Achieved. -36% (16 out of 45) of all PCU and PIU staff are women. Data Source: Project progress reports. End of project impact evaluation.

Output: Environmental services in cross-border tourism centers improved. Indicator: That Sikhottabong 2km internal road and drainage upgrade, solid waste transfer station, tourist information enter, and 10 hectares of rehabilitated urban greeen space with flood protection benefiting 35,000 residents in Thakhek City. Progress/Status: Achieved. - The contract TIIG-LAO-W01 was signed on 29 May 2017 with Dala Construction Sole Co. Ltd at a contract cost of $1,899,815.85 and the contractor mobilized in July 2017 (combined with work at Xang Cave 1-a.).
- Physical progress is 100%. Handover of the construction site was on 6 September 2019. Data Source: End of project impact evaluation. Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity to promote inclusive tourism growth strengthened. Indicator: 40% of DMO management positions are held by women Achievement: 43 Progress/Status: Substantially achieved. - 9 out of 23 (39%) DMN board members are women. - Women (including ethnic women) have been appointed to DMNs and enabling conditions were created for their participation, such as: (i) encourage women to be candidate; and (ii) put quota of 40% for women for DMN.
Data Source: Project Progress Reports

Output: Institutional capacity to promote inclusive tourism growth strengthened. Indicator: 50% of 500 operators have access to the support are women Progress/Status: Achieved. - Over 50% of these SMEs are women-led. A high proportion of employees of these SMEs are women.
- A total 577 SME units related tourism and handicraft, out of which 339 (67%) women-owned/led, received direct support from the project, out of which 195 SME units, out of which 117 (60%) women-owned/led, also received materials and/or equipment in addition to capacity building and training, to upgrade production and product and service quality were women. Data Source: Project Progress Reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity to promote inclusive tourism growth strengthened. Indicator: 50% of 6,000 people reached by awareness raising activities are women Progress/Status: Achieved. - 3,831 (55%) out of 6,916 reached by awareness raising activities are women.
Data Source: Project Progress Reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity to promote inclusive tourism growth strengthened. Indicator: 8 Destination Management Organizations (DMOs) formed with systems and procedures in place to implement destination management plans Achievement: 8 Progress/Status: Substantially achieved. - Eight DMNs formed: Five DMNs directly formed by the project, one national and four in the target provinces, and three additional through collaboration with development partners in Bolikhamxay, Xieng Khouang and Luang Namtha provinces.
- Approved destination management plans (DMPs) at national level and in target provinces.
- National-level DMN task forces created covering marketing, tourism management, hospitality skills, and product development.
- National-level DMN meetings held twice a year, and in the target provinces 1-2 times per year.
- DMN secretariats and taskforces receive regular training and capacity building assistance. Data Source: Project Progress Reports

Output: Institutional capacity to promote inclusive tourism growth strengthened. Indicator: At least 5 service enterprises are operating tourist attractions under a public-private partnership. Progress/Status: Achieved. O&M manuals for project supported tourist facilities prepared include the following PPP. As of 31 December 2021 4 out of 5 PPPs have been established.
Khammouane: (i) Sikhottabong Stupa: operation of the restaurant/café at the tourism information center established.
Luang Prabang: (ii) Operation of the tourist information center at the ferry pier: PPP established. (iii) operation of aspects of the pottery center (reception center): awaiting applications for operation under PPP; (iv) Operation of the tourist information centers and parking areas in Ban Xang Hai: PPP established; (v) Operation of the tourist information centers and parking areas in Ban Pak Ou: PPP established. Data Source: Project Progress Reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity to promote inclusive tourism growth strengthened. Indicator: At least 80% of newly constructed vendor space allocated to women. Achievement: 87 Progress/Status: Achieved. - The project has constructed space for 66 vendors, out of which 63 (95%) are allocated to women.
- Stall operators (majority are women) at That Sikhottabong and Xang Cave in Khammouane, in Ban Xieng Mene, Chom Phet and Pak Ou, Luang Prabang, and Chom Ong Cave, Oudomxay, will return to/move into original/new retail space after construction is completed. Data Source: Project Progress Reports

Output: Institutional capacity to promote inclusive tourism growth strengthened. Indicator: Operator of 500 small and medium-sized enterprise operators (50% of whom are women) gain access to professional tourism-related business support services and micro-finance. Progress/Status: Achieved. - The project has supported a series of capacity building activities and tourist-related business support services for SMEs operating in the tourism sector. Support was based on the destination management plans and needs assessments.
- 577 SME units related tourism and handicraft, out of which 339 (67%) women-owned/led, received direct support from the project, out of which 195 SME units, out of which 117 (60%) women-owned/led, also received materials and/or equipment in addition to capacity building and training, to upgrade production and product and service quality were women. Data Source: Project Progress Reports Actual value:

Output: Last-mile tourism access infrastructure improved. Indicator: Chom Ong Cave 54.0 km paved rural access road and tourism constructed and benefiting at least 8,000 residents. Achievement: 35 Progress/Status: Achieved. Engineer's cost estimates for this civil work package exceeded available loan proceeds at the time of advertisement, thus the scope in bidding documents was reduced from 54 km road circuit to 39 km western section with cave access. In Oct 2018, ADB approved the EA's request to use loan savings resulted from lower than estimated bid prices for 3 works contracts and unallocated funds to finance the remaining 16km road circuit.
(i) Contract TIIG-LAO-W02 (39 km road section) was signed with Chitchareune Construction Co., Ltd on 17 Nov 2017 at a contract cost of $9,566,034.88. Contractor was mobilized in December 2017. - Physical progress is 100%. Handover of the construction site was on 29 Jan 2021.
(ii) Contract TIIG-LAO-W02a (16 km road section) to complete the circuit road was signed with 68 Trading Construction and Service Joint Stock Company on 25 September 2019 at a contract cost of $4,035,448.91 and contractor mobilized in October 2019. - Physical progress is 100%. - Final inspection was conducted in Jul 2021. - Handover of the construction site was in August 2021.
Data Source: Project progress reports. Completion report. End of project impact evaluation.

Output: Last-mile tourism access infrastructure improved. Indicator: Chomphet Heritage District 2.2 km paved access road, ferry terminal, and upgraded river piers constructed and benefiting at least 2,100 residents. Achievement: 2.2 Progress/Status: Achieved - Contract TIIG-LAO-W03 was signed with R8CE-PKCC-TSC J/V on 11 Oct 2017 at a contract cost of $4,563,596.36 and contractor was mobilized in Nov 2017 (combined with 1-c.).
- Physical progress is 100%. Handover of the construction site was on 8 September 2020. Data Source: Project progress reports. Completion report. End of project impact evaluation.

Output: Last-mile tourism access infrastructure improved. Indicator: Xang Cave 4 km paved access road and amenities constructed and benefiting 1,900 residents. Ltd at a contract cost of $1,899,815.85 and the contractor mobilized in July 2017 (combined with work at That Sikhottabong2-a.).

Achievement: 10 Progress/Status: Achieved - Contract TIIG-LAO-W03 was signed with R8CE-PKCC-TSC J/V on 11 Oct 2017 at a contract cost of $4,563,596.36 and contractor was mobilized in Nov 2017 (combined with 1-b.).
- Physical progress is 100%. Handover of the construction site was on 8 September 2020. Data Source: Project progress reports. Completion report. End of project impact evaluation.

Output: Effective project implementation and knowledge management. Indicator: At least 3 joint marketing activities undertaken annually in cooperation with another GMS country. Achievement: 10 Progress/Status: Achieved. An average of 3.6 joint marketing activities (18 activities in 5 years) undertaken annually in cooperation with another GMS country events.
2016 - 2016 ASEAN Ecotourism Forum, Pakse, Lao PDR - 2016 Mekong Tourism Forum, Sihanoukville, Cambodia with the theme “Authentic Experiences along the Mekong River”.
2017 - Lane Xang Heritage Quadrangle cultural routes maps published jointly with Thailand - Lane Xang Heritage Quadrangle cooperation meetings, surveys and promotional materials produced - 2017 Mekong Tourism Forum, Luang Prabang, Lao PDR, with the theme “Prosper with Purpose”
Data Source: Project progress reports. GMS TWG Summary of Proceedings

Output: Effective project implementation and knowledge management. Indicator: Collection and reporting of tourism statistics by all GMS NTOs in a harmonized format. Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. The Mekong Tourism Coordinating Office (MTCO) organized a number of GMS tourism statistics harmonization workshops in 2017, 2018 and 2019 in which NTOS from GMS countries, including MICT, participated. As a result, definitions and formats for 20 key GMS tourism indicators have been agreed between the NTOs and MTCO, and MTCO tracks and reports on these 20 indicators annually: https://www.mekongtourism.org/about/tourism-performance/. Data Source: Project progress reports. GMS TWG Summary of Proceedings Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
